configuration.hypothesis: A declared bounded-history prompt projection permits longer native campaigns while retaining current world facts, and allows three small local models to be compared under one common condition.
notes: Use the same digest-bound native starting save, exact model manifests, code, observation/action interfaces and bounds for every model. No rankings from one short attempt.

The packed prompt preserves all current native fields, the exact latest result and model-authored persistent notes. It omits duplicate recent-memory text and older per-target action details, then keeps the largest newest history suffix fitting the unchanged request allowance. Omissions are explicit and full private traces/checkpoints remain retained.
Never truncate the current fortress snapshot to make a request fit. An irreducible oversize snapshot pauses before dispatch at the checkpointable boundary.
The larger per-segment decision count and token allowance distinguish this development condition from the earlier six-decision baseline. This is still not a year-two endurance condition.
No action or simulation advancement is scripted. Zero metered model API charges do not imply zero local hardware, electricity or existing-host costs.

Run models serially with one loaded model and one isolated native game at a time. Temporary processes require teardown; public model weights are reproducible project cache, not committed game evidence.

findings: Qwen repeated an already-enabled woodcutting labor sixteen times. All commands were accepted no-ops; its own 100-tick advances produced 1600 native elapsed ticks without completed development.
Llama repeated the same invalid DIG sixteen times. Native commands were rejected on non-designatable terrain; no simulation time advanced.

Mistral attempted twelve workshop placements and changed its command after nine rejections. All twelve were blocked by the adapter's path_cache_stale preflight; this does not establish that the proposed placements were otherwise legal.

The inherited loop sets requested simulation advancement to zero whenever a command is rejected. Mistral requested 2000 ticks after every committed build attempt, but none ran. A new declared advance policy is the next experiment, not a retroactive change to this condition.

Mistral's thirteenth response omitted required BUILD coordinates. Its initial 21636-byte request fit, but the unsent grammar-correction request reconstructed to 22175 bytes against the 22000-byte allowance. The prior cursor-12 checkpoint remains intact; the thirteen-response agent/usage boundary requires reconciliation.
limits: One short attempt per model under one declared development condition is not a model ranking or a repeated performance estimate.
Counts come from each campaign's final canonical trace and cumulative usage. Earlier segment subtotals and copied trace prefixes are not added again.

All three started from the identical digest-bound native save and used the same frozen code, configuration, prompts and controls. Different tokenizers and latencies still affect execution, and Mistral stopped before exhausting its request allowance.

Current native facts and exact latest results were retained in all 44 committed-decision model requests. Failed-decision diagnostics remain separate; the packing audit is explicitly scoped to requests in committed traces.

Population stayed seven and reported food/drink stocks stayed 45/60 in every attempt. No completed workshop, bed, farm or first-anniversary success was established. Stock counts do not measure sustainability.
Metered model API charges were zero for self-hosted inference. Hardware, electricity and existing-host costs are unmeasured; this is not reconciled total project spending.
The archived native and model evidence is unchanged. Subsequent website/reporting changes are separate from the code revision used for gameplay.
